title: Suggestions
intro: Improvements to the site and to the decision process, written so a reviewer can choose a path rather than inherit one. Each card states the problem, the options with effort and risk, what each option unlocks, and a recommendation. Nothing here is implemented; each card ends in the decision a reviewer has to make.
scoring_note: Effort: S = a day or less, M = a week, L = a month or a data purchase. Impact: how much it changes a decision. Risk: what could go wrong or be misread. Recommendation is the author's, and it is the shortest path to a decision, not the most impressive one.

items.title: Score against a real price instead of the reference line
items.problem: Every economic gate compares the model with a naive reference line built from the same inputs. That measures whether the model's refinements bite, not whether it beats a market. A +3.0 'edge' can be entirely an artefact of the reference being naive.

options.name: Licensed odds archive
options.risk: Cost, licensing scope, survivorship of closing lines
options.unlocks: True closing-line value, real ROI, real G3/G4

options.name: Dated manual quote snapshots
options.risk: Human transcription error, limited coverage, timezone mistakes
options.unlocks: A defensible first price series you can audit line by line

options.name: Keep the reference line and rename the metric
options.risk: None, but no economic claim is possible

items.recommendation: Start with dated manual snapshots (S) to prove the pipeline end-to-end, and run the archive purchase in parallel. Never call a reference-line difference an edge in the UI; the site already avoids that, and it is the right call.

items.title: Grow the out-of-sample window past 100 graded games before reading anything into the leaderboard
items.problem: The top strategy has 23 graded plays. At that size a 16-7 run happens by chance often enough that the exact p is 0.093. The ranking is therefore not informative, and any ranking shown at n = 23 is a false signal.

options.name: Let the daily refresh accumulate
options.risk: Slow; the league plays ~6-8 games a night across a 3-day horizon

options.name: Backfill earlier games
options.risk: Ratings would have to be rebuilt point-in-time or look-ahead leaks in

options.name: Show the leaderboard only as a queue

items.recommendation: Both: let it accumulate, and backfill only with strictly point-in-time ratings. Until then, present the leaderboard as 'not yet rankable' rather than numbering it — the tier cap already implies that.

items.title: Capture the full 465-row player table, not the top 50
items.problem: Injury impact is a lower bound because minutes are known for 50 of 465 players. Roster minutes coverage sits at 27-30%, so most absences are counted as zero impact. That is honest but nearly useless for the games where the absent player is a bench starter.

options.name: Capture all 10 pages of the players table
options.risk: Ten fetches per refresh; markup fragility
options.unlocks: Real minute shares, real availability deltas

options.name: Leave the bound and label it

items.recommendation: Capture all 10 pages first: it is the cheapest large improvement in the whole repository and it turns a lower bound into a number.

items.title: Move injury capture to a pre-tip cadence and record the report version
items.problem: This session saw seven status changes between the 17:15 and 19:30 ET editions. A once-daily snapshot at 17:30 ET would have published four Questionables as likely participants and one Probable as playing.

options.name: Two sweeps a day (mid-afternoon, 2h before first tip)
options.unlocks: Status change history, which is itself a signal

options.name: Keep one snapshot but timestamp it loudly
options.risk: Known-stale data in a fast-moving market

items.recommendation: Two sweeps, and publish the status *history* (the diff between editions) as a first-class table. The diff is more informative than either snapshot.

items.title: Fit the availability coefficient empirically instead of assuming 15 net-rating points
items.problem: The injury impact coefficient (15 points per 100 possessions if a team's whole rotation were out) and the 0.6 offense share are modelling choices. A sensitivity band is published, but the headline number is still an assumption.

options.name: Regress team net rating on unavailable minute share
options.risk: Confounded by who the unavailable player is
options.unlocks: An estimated coefficient with a standard error

options.name: Use on/off splits per player
options.risk: Small samples per player, lineup collinearity

options.name: Keep the band
options.risk: A wide interval that cannot price anything

items.recommendation: Estimate the team-level coefficient first; it is a single number and it immediately converts an assumption into a measured quantity with an interval.

items.title: Pre-register strategies and correct for multiplicity
items.problem: Ten strategies were evaluated. At alpha = 0.05 across ten tests, roughly half a false positive is expected even if none of them works. The reported p-values are unadjusted.

options.name: Pre-register before each week's games
options.risk: Needs discipline and a fixed rule

items.recommendation: Do both. Adjustment is a one-line change to the validation output and pre-registration is a text file committed before tip — neither is expensive, and together they are the difference between a lab and a lottery.

items.title: Make the gate status the primary visual, not the record
items.problem: A reader scanning a leaderboard sees 16-7 and +7.55 units first. That is the most misleading pair of numbers on the site, because n = 23 and the skill gate fails.

options.name: Sort by gate status, then by score
options.risk: The flashiest strategy is not on top
options.unlocks: Readers seeing the verdict before the record

options.name: Show record only inside a closed detail row

items.recommendation: Sort by gate count passed, then by score, and put the record beside the sample size in the same cell. This exact change is implemented on the new Command Center leaderboard page so it can be judged side by side with the old one.

items.title: One command center, two labs, no dead ends
items.problem: The repository now contains two independently built labs (one at the root, one under docs/b) and neither linked to the other. A reviewer had no way in.

options.name: A single navigation shell over both
options.risk: Two visual languages on one site

options.name: Merge the two labs into one
Keep them separate and document it

items.recommendation: A nav shell now (implemented), a merge later only if the second lab earns its place. The shell is a one-file change per page and it buys the whole site.

items.title: Add a settlement ledger so every pick is graded against what was actually available
items.problem: Every upcoming pick is PENDING and nothing in the repository grades a real price. Without a ledger the site can never compute a live ROI, so the competition cannot pay out.

options.name: Append-only settlement file per play
options.unlocks: Live ROI, closing-line value, a real leaderboard

options.name: Grade only the model, never a price

items.recommendation: An append-only settlement ledger keyed by game id and market, written before tip and locked after. It is the minimum viable thing that makes the competition real.

items.title: Define the reward schedule and retire rule in writing
items.problem: The leaderboard has tiers but no rewards, and four strategies generate zero plays. Both are policy gaps, not code gaps, and they will be filled by accident if nobody decides.

options.name: Gate-first payout tiers, published before launch
options.risk: Fewer payouts than a naive design

items.recommendation: Gate-first tiers, published with a written retire rule ('no qualifying play for 30 days, or a gate regression, retires the strategy'). Publish retired strategies too; a leaderboard that only shows live winners is not a leaderboard.
